audit_status.review_note: Reviewed for Joseph's favored status, kethonet passim, dreams, brothers' hatred, pit, sale to Ishmaelites/Midianites, dipped garment, and Jacob's mourning. Compact verse layer for app ingestion.

verses.restored: Jacob dwelled in the land of his father’s sojournings, in the land of Canaan.

familiar.text: And Jacob dwelt in the land wherein his father was a stranger, in the land of Canaan.

modern.text: Now Jacob lived in the land where his father had resided, the land of Canaan.

original.text: וַיֵּ֣שֶׁב יַעֲקֹ֔ב בְּאֶ֖רֶץ מְגוּרֵ֣י אָבִ֑יו בְּאֶ֖רֶץ כְּנָֽעַן

verses.restored: These are the generations of Jacob. Joseph, seventeen years old, was shepherding the flock with his brothers, and Joseph brought a bad report of them to their father.

familiar.text: These are the generations of Jacob. Joseph, being seventeen years old, was feeding the flock with his brethren; and the lad was with the sons of Bilhah, and with the sons of Zilpah, his father’s wives: and Joseph brought unto his father their evil report.

modern.text: This is the account of Jacob. When Joseph was seventeen years old, he was tending the flock with his brothers, the sons of his father’s wives Bilhah and Zilpah, and he brought their father a bad report about them.

original.text: אֵ֣לֶּה תֹּלְד֣וֹת יַעֲקֹ֗ב יוֹסֵ֞ף בֶּן שְׁבַֽע עֶשְׂרֵ֤ה שָׁנָה֙ הָיָ֨ה רֹעֶ֤ה אֶת אֶחָיו֙ בַּצֹּ֔אן וְה֣וּא נַ֗עַר אֶת בְּנֵ֥י בִלְהָ֛ה וְאֶת בְּנֵ֥י זִלְפָּ֖ה נְשֵׁ֣י אָבִ֑יו וַיָּבֵ֥א יוֹסֵ֛ף אֶת דִּבָּתָ֥ם רָעָ֖ה אֶל אֲבִיהֶֽם

verses.restored: Israel loved Joseph more than all his sons, because he was a son of his old age, and he made him a long ornamented tunic.

familiar.text: Now Israel loved Joseph more than all his children, because he was the son of his old age: and he made him a coat of many colours.

modern.text: Now Israel loved Joseph more than his other sons, because Joseph had been born to him in his old age; so he made him a robe of many colors.

original.text: וְיִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל אָהַ֤ב אֶת יוֹסֵף֙ מִכָּל בָּנָ֔יו כִּֽי בֶן זְקֻנִ֥ים ה֖וּא ל֑וֹ וְעָ֥שָׂה ל֖וֹ כְּתֹ֥נֶת פַּסִּֽים

verses.restored: His brothers saw that their father loved him more than all his brothers, so they hated him and could not speak peaceably to him.

familiar.text: And when his brethren saw that their father loved him more than all his brethren, they hated him, and could not speak peaceably unto him.

modern.text: When Joseph’s brothers saw that their father loved him more than any of them, they hated him and could not speak a kind word to him.

verses.restored: Joseph dreamed a dream and told it to his brothers, and they hated him even more.

familiar.text: And Joseph dreamed a dream, and he told it his brethren: and they hated him yet the more.

modern.text: Then Joseph had a dream, and when he told it to his brothers, they hated him even more.

familiar.text: For, behold, we were binding sheaves in the field, and, lo, my sheaf arose, and also stood upright; and, behold, your sheaves stood round about, and made obeisance to my sheaf.

verses.restored: His brothers said to him, Will you really reign over us? Will you truly rule us? They hated him even more because of his dreams and his words.

familiar.text: And his brethren said to him, Shalt thou indeed reign over us? or shalt thou indeed have dominion over us? And they hated him yet the more for his dreams, and for his words.

modern.text: “Do you intend to reign over us?” his brothers asked. “Will you actually rule us?” So they hated him even more because of his dream and his statements.

familiar.text: And he dreamed yet another dream, and told it his brethren, and said, Behold, I have dreamed a dream more; and, behold, the sun and the moon and the eleven stars made obeisance to me.

modern.text: Then Joseph had another dream and told it to his brothers. “Look,” he said, “I had another dream, and this time the sun and moon and eleven stars were bowing down to me.”

verses.restored: Midianite traders passed by. They drew Joseph up from the pit and sold Joseph to the Ishmaelites for twenty pieces of silver, and they brought Joseph to Egypt.

familiar.text: Then there passed by Midianites merchantmen; and they drew and lifted up Joseph out of the pit, and sold Joseph to the Ishmeelites for twenty pieces of silver: and they brought Joseph into Egypt.

modern.text: So when the Midianite traders passed by, his brothers pulled Joseph out of the pit and sold him for twenty shekels of silver to the Ishmaelites, who took him to Egypt.

original.text: וַיַּֽעַבְרוּ֩ אֲנָשִׁ֨ים מִדְיָנִ֜ים סֹֽחֲרִ֗ים וַֽיִּמְשְׁכוּ֙ וַיַּֽעֲל֤וּ אֶת יוֹסֵף֙ מִן הַבּ֔וֹר וַיִּמְכְּר֧וּ אֶת יוֹסֵ֛ף לַיִּשְׁמְעֵאלִ֖ים בְּעֶשְׂרִ֣ים כָּ֑סֶף וַיָּבִ֥יאוּ אֶת יוֹסֵ֖ף מִצְרָֽיְמָה

verses.restored: Reuben returned to the pit, and look, Joseph was not in the pit. He tore his garments.

familiar.text: And Reuben returned unto the pit; and, behold, Joseph was not in the pit; and he rent his clothes.

modern.text: When Reuben returned to the pit and saw that Joseph was not there, he tore his clothes,

original.text: וַיָּ֤שָׁב רְאוּבֵן֙ אֶל הַבּ֔וֹר וְהִנֵּ֥ה אֵין יוֹסֵ֖ף בַּבּ֑וֹר וַיִּקְרַ֖ע אֶת בְּגָדָֽיו

verses.restored: He returned to his brothers and said, The boy is gone, and I, where can I go?

familiar.text: And he returned unto his brethren, and said, The child is not; and I, whither shall I go?

modern.text: returned to his brothers, and said, “The boy is gone! What am I going to do?” Jacob Mourns Joseph

original.text: וַיָּ֥שָׁב אֶל אֶחָ֖יו וַיֹּאמַ֑ר הַיֶּ֣לֶד אֵינֶ֔נּוּ וַאֲנִ֖י אָ֥נָה אֲנִי בָֽא

verses.restored: They took Joseph’s tunic, slaughtered a male goat, and dipped the tunic in the blood.

familiar.text: And they took Joseph’s coat, and killed a kid of the goats, and dipped the coat in the blood;

modern.text: Then they took Joseph’s robe, slaughtered a young goat, and dipped the robe in its blood.

original.text: וַיִּקְח֖וּ אֶת כְּתֹ֣נֶת יוֹסֵ֑ף וַֽיִּשְׁחֲטוּ֙ שְׂעִ֣יר עִזִּ֔ים וַיִּטְבְּל֥וּ אֶת הַכֻּתֹּ֖נֶת בַּדָּֽם

verses.restored: They sent the long ornamented tunic and brought it to their father, saying, We found this. Recognize, please, whether it is your son’s tunic or not.

familiar.text: And they sent the coat of many colours, and they brought it to their father; and said, This have we found: know now whether it be thy son’s coat or no.

modern.text: They sent the robe of many colors to their father and said, “We found this. Examine it to see whether it is your son’s robe or not.”

original.text: וַֽיְשַׁלְּח֞וּ אֶת כְּתֹ֣נֶת הַפַּסִּ֗ים וַיָּבִ֨יאוּ֙ אֶל אֲבִיהֶ֔ם וַיֹּאמְר֖וּ זֹ֣את מָצָ֑אנוּ הַכֶּר נָ֗א הַכְּתֹ֧נֶת בִּנְךָ֛ הִ֖וא אִם לֹֽא

verses.restored: He recognized it and said, It is my son’s tunic. A wild animal has devoured him; Joseph is surely torn apart.

familiar.text: And he knew it, and said, It is my son’s coat; an evil beast hath devoured him; Joseph is without doubt rent in pieces.

modern.text: His father recognized it and said, “It is my son’s robe! A vicious animal has devoured him. Joseph has surely been torn to pieces!”

original.text: וַיַּכִּירָ֤הּ וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ כְּתֹ֣נֶת בְּנִ֔י חַיָּ֥ה רָעָ֖ה אֲכָלָ֑תְהוּ טָרֹ֥ף טֹרַ֖ף יוֹסֵֽף

verses.restored: Jacob tore his garments, put sackcloth on his loins, and mourned for his son many days.

familiar.text: And Jacob rent his clothes, and put sackcloth upon his loins, and mourned for his son many days.

modern.text: Then Jacob tore his clothes, put sackcloth around his waist, and mourned for his son many days.

original.text: וַיִּקְרַ֤ע יַעֲקֹב֙ שִׂמְלֹתָ֔יו וַיָּ֥שֶׂם שַׂ֖ק בְּמָתְנָ֑יו וַיִּתְאַבֵּ֥ל עַל בְּנ֖וֹ יָמִ֥ים רַבִּֽים

verses.restored: All his sons and all his daughters rose to comfort him, but he refused to be comforted and said, I will go down to Sheol mourning to my son. His father wept for him.

familiar.text: And all his sons and all his daughters rose up to comfort him; but he refused to be comforted; and he said, For I will go down into the grave unto my son mourning. Thus his father wept for him.

modern.text: All his sons and daughters tried to comfort him, but he refused to be comforted. “No,” he said. “I will go down to Sheol mourning for my son.” So his father wept for him.

original.text: וַיָּקֻמוּ֩ כָל בָּנָ֨יו וְכָל בְּנֹתָ֜יו לְנַחֲמ֗וֹ וַיְמָאֵן֙ לְהִתְנַחֵ֔ם וַיֹּ֕אמֶר כִּֽי אֵרֵ֧ד אֶל בְּנִ֛י אָבֵ֖ל שְׁאֹ֑לָה וַיֵּ֥בְךְּ אֹת֖וֹ אָבִֽיו

verses.restored: The Midianites sold him in Egypt to Potiphar, an officer of Pharaoh, captain of the guard.

familiar.text: And the Midianites sold him into Egypt unto Potiphar, an officer of Pharaoh’s, and captain of the guard.

modern.text: Meanwhile, the Midianites sold Joseph in Egypt to Potiphar, an officer of Pharaoh and captain of the guard.

original.text: וְהַ֨מְּדָנִ֔ים מָכְר֥וּ אֹת֖וֹ אֶל מִצְרָ֑יִם לְפֽוֹטִיפַר֙ סְרִ֣יס פַּרְעֹ֔ה שַׂ֖ר הַטַּבָּחִֽים
